Event: `ee2eb98a6555ede360649a916cee9685` · 2026-09-24T18:05:45Z

> K5 plan v1 red-team review. Read-only; code at wp-k5 08848f60a; wp-k5-unreviewed not inspected. Checked against WP-K5 acceptance, R10/R12/I13-I15, RESOURCES Scheduling/Timer, TENETS 3, answer 166 and the 7 resolved K5-q answers.
> 
> VERDICT: BLOCK. v2 must fix P1-1..P1-3 and should fold the P2s. P1-2 needs an orchestrator rule, because it narrows the approved K5-q-minimum answer that 'a new budget enters at the floor'.
> 
> P1-1 Charging choke point is incomplete; there is a free-CPU channel. The plan charges only in activate_process_thread, but several deschedules never pass through it:
> - thread_exit: destroy_thread -> switch_to_thread (services.rs:1852).
> - process_exit, faulted and a kill of the running process: end_process -> terminate_process -> switch_to_thread(parent) (process.rs:584, services.rs:2281).
> - finish_callback_and_resume and make_callback_to (services.rs:672/728).
> Attack: a user budget loops thread_create -> spin SLICE-e -> thread_exit, or does the same with child processes that exit or fault. No run is ever charged, so the budget's share is unbounded.
> Fix: account at the trap boundary. At every U-mode trap entry, charge (now - last return to U) to the budget of the process that ran (read before any teardown), or hook every current-(pid,tid) change including switch_to_thread. Add the boot attack case sched-exit-churn (thread churn plus process exit/fault churn; victim share >= w/W - tol) and a model mutation (e.g. R12ExitRunsFree).
> 
> P1-2 Budget churn sheds pass debt. A new budget enters at the floor, ranked as a waker (ahead of the queued budget at the minimum). Its first slice is charged to a budget that is then destroyed, and the carved weight returns to the parent.
> Attack: any holder of a user budget handle loops: budget_create(weight 1), spawn a spinner, let it run one full SLICE, budget_destroy, repeat. Each cycle costs a few syscalls plus an image copy and gains 10 ms. A weight-1 child takes about half the CPU from a weight-100 victim. That breaks 'a spinning budget cannot delay another beyond its weight' and RESOURCES 'always gets at least its share'.
> Pre-charging at creation is not enough: a pre-charge made at creation vanishes if the first wake comes after the floor has passed it (max(own, floor)), so budgets created early and started later get the free slice anyway.
> Options for the orchestrator:
> (a) Entry fee at the first wake: pass = floor + SLICE*STRIDE/weight.
> (b) Bill a destroyed budget's excess pass to the budget of its destroyer or creator. This is awkward for kernel-deadline destruction.
> (c) Other.
> Whatever the rule, add the sched-budget-churn boot case, create/destroy churn in the model fairness generator, and a mutation.
> 
> P1-3 Entry-time expiry kills or invalidates state the trap handler already captured (I14 panics):
> (a) kmain's own SwitchTo is a legacy ecall from PID 1 (main.rs:144). Expiry at that entry can destroy the picked process through a budget deadline, and then activate_process_thread fails at expect('couldn't switch to pid'), which panics.
> (b) trap_handler reads pid = current_pid() once (irq.rs:192) and uses it later for PREVIOUS_PAIR (irq.rs:290), redoubt::handle, syscall::handle and faulted. If expiry at entry kills the current process, all of those name a dead PID.
> Fix:
> - PID-1 entries never expire. kmain runs expire -> reconcile -> pick -> SwitchTo with nothing in between, and a failed SwitchTo re-picks instead of panicking.
> - At a U-mode entry, expire first, then re-read current. If the entering thread died, skip the syscall's work and resume current. For an IRQ entry, re-read after expiry before recording PREVIOUS_PAIR.
> - Write this per entry kind in v2: Redoubt, legacy, external IRQ, timer, RETURN_FROM_ISR, EXIT_THREAD, fault.
> 
> P2 and P3 follow in the next reply.

> P2-1 Deadlines during legacy callbacks. The plan unmasks the timer during callbacks and lets expiry run there. Today no Redoubt call, including budget_destroy, runs in_irq (redoubt.rs:48,52), so the following is newly reachable. A lease deadline that kills the interrupted process saved in PREVIOUS_PAIR leads finish_isr to finish_callback_and_resume(dead pid), and expect('unable to resume previous PID') panics (irq.rs:113). Killing the callback owner (the current process) mid-callback is also unhandled.
> Fix: defer budget-deadline destruction while PREVIOUS_PAIR is set (timeouts may still expire), run it right after finish_isr's resume, and handle a doomed previous process there.
> Also, the Risks line saying 'a callback can't hold off slice ends' contradicts the deferral of slice end to finish_isr: a callback that never returns keeps the CPU. State that as a residual until K6, with the grants evidence that only manifest processes can claim IRQs. The forced-yield path must not expect SWITCHTO_CALLER (it is None in a callback started from idle).
> 
> P2-2 The deadline path is not caller-less. The interrupted current process may be in the doomed subtree, so it must be killed last as the caller (caller_doomed -> Resume). Budget::destroy(.., None) as written would kill it mid-loop, and kill_process asserts target != current.
> sched::Hart.running must be a (frame, id) BudgetRef with a liveness check. Settle its partial slice before destroy_marked frees the frame, so that no pass, rem or queued word is written into a freed or reused frame. Purge the queued set too.
> 
> P2-3 Kernel work is billed to whoever was running. Charging measures wall time between switches, so a timer interrupt's expiry walk (find_thread over 64x31 threads per due thread, message.rs:1554) and deadline destruction (several O(frames) sweeps, budget.rs:665/698, message.rs:1486) are charged to the interrupted victim.
> Attacks: (1) the maximum number of threads sleeping with deadlines staggered 1 µs apart; (2) staggered lease deadlines. Each costs the attacker one cheap syscall and costs the victim an interrupt, a walk and a re-pick.
> Fix: charge user time plus the budget's own syscall time; do not charge interrupt or timer handler time. Add a timer-flood case (victim share >= w/W - tol).
> 
> P2-4 Tests that would not catch regressions:
> (a) timeouts only reports lateness. If the timeout-arming code broke, the spinner sub-case would still pass on the 10 ms slice-end interrupts. Assert a lateness bound well below SLICE, with deadlines offset from slice ends.
> (b) sched-ties grades the kernel against its own printed 'rank reason'. Dump raw records instead (entry sequence, event, budget, pass, tie) and compute the verdict in the checker.
> (c) The 200-iteration reply race must show both rows at least once and check that the server's disposition matches (delivered with Success; discarded with Timeout, consumed and exactly one notice).
> (d) Nothing covers P1-1 or P1-2.
> 
> P2-5 Legacy direct switches (borrowed-quantum send_message) run another budget with no pick, and the model has none of them. Define Hart.running as the budget actually running (a direct switch deschedules the old budget and runs the new one), and list this as an out-of-model residual until K6.

> 3. Round-robin within a budget differs: the kernel uses a (pid,tid) cursor, the model a wake-order VecDeque (sched.rs:53-66). State the difference and accept it, or align them; the differential doesn't cover it.

Event: `77b2f3ed8819c3aa75c345403871ab88` · 2026-09-24T18:06:15Z

> K5 plan v2: answer every finding in K5-plan-review (red BLOCK: P1-1..3, the P2s and P3s), on top of v1.1. Still PLAN ONLY. Orchestrator rule for P1-2 (budget churn), a proposed R12/R7 clarification that the owner confirms at plan approval: a pass is inherited through the budget tree.
> - At creation, a new budget's pass = max(floor, its PARENT BUDGET's pass). Not the creator process's budget: the tree parent whose weight it carves (R7).
> - At destroy (budget_destroy, deadline, or revocation), the parent budget's pass = max(parent pass, child pass), so the child's unpaid debt moves up the tree and isn't dropped. Apply it bottom-up for a destroyed subtree, in R10 order.
> - A parent budget that holds no process never runs, so debt parked on it only raises the entry pass of its next children. The floor catches up over time; there is no permanent penalty.
> - Why not an entry fee: it's an arbitrary constant, and it taxes legitimate short-lived budgets. Why not bill the creator: the steward would inherit user leases' debt and slow down lease termination.
> - Show that it closes the loop: create, run one slice, destroy, repeat gains nothing over just running in the parent. Add a boot case sched-budget-churn and a model mutation (drop the debt on destroy, and/or enter at the floor only). Check it against carving: weight returns to the parent at destroy (R7), and the pass must not be double-counted.
> Other P1s: take the red team's fixes, or better ones, with proof. P1-1: account at trap entry and exit (every deschedule path, including thread_exit, exit, fault, kill and callback switches), with sched-exit-churn and a mutation. P1-3: no expiry on the PID-1/kmain legacy entries; re-read current after expiry; no expect() on a pid that expiry may have killed.
> P2s: if the legacy callback and finish_isr paths can't be made safe before K6, say so and exclude them explicitly, with a guard, not a panic. Bill kernel handler work to the kernel, not the victim, or bound it and say so. Make every acceptance test assert, not just report (lateness gets a bound; ties are checked against an independent oracle, not the scheduler's own ordering).
> P3s: fix the contradictions with the answers (the rank direction is the one v1.1 chose; fence placement per v1.1; spec edits are in the docs commit).
> Post v2 as one consolidated reply on K5-plan listing each finding and its disposition, then complete the assignment.

> N1 (P1) Carve inflation: the stride weight is unspecified, and the model uses the limit. v2 never says which weight goes into step = t/w. The model schedules at the budget's limit and never updates it on carving (model/src/kernel.rs:856 add_budget(id, l.weight)). The kernel stores limit and carved separately (budget.rs:74-89).
> Attack: user U (weight 100) holds processes and carves child C with weight 100 (allowed: weight <= free). Spinners run in both. Both count 100, so the subtree gets 2/3 against a weight-100 victim, and nesting to MAX_DEPTH gives d/(d+1). R6 doesn't touch this because the budgets run concurrently. It breaks 'cannot delay another beyond its weight' and RESOURCES 'weight is carved like pages'.
> Rule needed: a budget's own stride weight = free weight (limit - carved), plus a rule for free weight 0 while it holds processes (refuse the carve, or its threads don't run). rem copes with weight changes, since t < 2^61 still holds.

> 
> N2 (P1) R6 lifts un-normalized debt across principals. Pass units scale with 1/weight. max(parent, child) lifts the pass of the deepest, lightest descendant, not the direct child's.
> Attack: U (weight 100) creates G (weight 1), runs one slice and destroys G, so U.pass is about floor + SLICE*STRIDE/1. At U's logout, lease end or deadline, users.pass becomes that value. The next child of users that the steward creates (another user's session or lease) enters at max(floor, users.pass). It can't run until the floor catches up, which takes about SLICE*sum(w_runnable)/1. Under the named workload (16x100 + 2x1000) that is about 36 s, and it repeats with every such destroy. v2's residual ('at most one slice at the child's weight; only init and steward create there at >= 100') is wrong because the lifted pass comes from the grandchild.
> Fix: normalize when propagating. parent.pass = max(parent.pass, f + ceil((child.pass - f)+ x w_child / w_parent)), where f = floor at destroy and w_parent = the parent's weight after the carve returns. The churn proof still holds: the lineage is charged r*STRIDE/w_P, as if the parent ran it. The u128 mul/div happens only at destroy (rv32 builtins).
> Add a boot case: a weight-1 grandchild's debt, then logout; a new sibling created by the launcher must run within a bound under spinners. Add a mutation for unnormalized propagation.
> 
> N3 (P2) Billing a batch to its first due item bills victims. At one instant, timeouts go first, in (pid,tid) order. An attacker that aligns many timeouts to a victim's predictable periodic deadline has all their fail_wait/pump work billed to the victim. Bill each item's processing to its own budget, and only the shared walk to the first item or to the kernel. Also start syscall_since after expire_due, so entry expiry isn't billed to the caller.
> 
> N4 (P2) The 'O(1) uncharged work per charged syscall' bound is misstated. Every spurious interrupt and hint recompute is a full walk: threads (64x31) plus, for the budget-deadline hint, every object frame (budgets are found by scanning 0..high_frame, as destroy_begin does at budget.rs:665), and the attacker grows that with pages. State the bound as O(T+F) per interrupt, or index budget deadlines (e.g. a list threaded through the frames).
> 
> N5 (P2) 'lateness <= 1 ms' is unsound on plain TCG. timeouts and budget-deadline aren't sched-* cases, so they run without icount, and a host preemption of the vCPU thread shows up as guest lateness. The bound is sound under fixed-shift icount with sleep=off, so run those two cases with it, or bound TCG at <= SLICE/2 (the A/B order check already proves per-deadline arming). The independent sched_oracle is sound under icount (it is order-only).
> 
> N6 (P3) The A/B check needs a gap t2-t1 larger than the entry handling time (so the two are separate entries) and much smaller than SLICE. It also has to exclude trials where a slice end falls between t1 and t2, because A then legitimately runs first. Use the trace or repeat-and-classify. Show that A and B both enter at the floor (a long prior sleep).

> N7 (P3) sched_oracle.rs in tools/testbench conflicts with the orchestrator's 18:11 answer limiting tools/testbench/** to the icount option. Get that confirmed.

> N8 (P3) ROOT_WEIGHT 1,000,000: mirror it in the model's boot limits (model/src/kernel.rs:114-116) and check cases that assert weight counters. At R6 creation, fold a running parent's pending time before reading its pass.

Event: `919c69a72544e05800a3ac1873a06928` · 2026-09-24T18:15:43Z

> K5 plan v3: answer the red team's v2 re-review (N1-N8 on K5-plan-review). Still PLAN ONLY. Orchestrator rulings, which the owner confirms at approval:
> N1 (carve inflation): a budget's stride weight is its FREE weight (its weight limit minus what it has carved to children), not its limit. So carving moves share and never duplicates it (R7). A carve that would leave a budget holding a process with free weight 0 is refused (budget_create returns the existing error for limits), consistent with R12's 'a weight-0 budget holds no process'. When a child is destroyed and its weight returns, the parent's stride weight rises at that moment; fold the pass first so earlier runtime is charged at the old weight. Add a case (a parent carving an equal child can't double its share, nested too) and a mutation (stride weight = limit).
> N2 (my rule was wrong: it lifted un-normalized debt): replace the destroy step with weight-normalized propagation: parent pass = max(parent pass, f + (child pass - f) x w_child / w_parent), where f = the floor and the weights are stride weights at destroy, using the same exact-remainder arithmetic as charging. Entry stays max(floor, parent pass): pass is virtual time, so inheriting a wait needs no scaling, but moving work does. Re-check the churn proof under both rulings, and add a case for the steward-creates-after-logout scenario the red team describes (a bound on the sibling's wait) plus a mutation (un-normalized lift).
> N3: bill expiry work per item to each item's own budget, not the batch to the first due item. N4: restate the uncharged-work bound truthfully (O(threads + object frames) walks), and say what bounds it per entry. N5: run the 1 ms lateness assertion under icount only; on plain TCG, report it. N6-N8: fix as the red team says. The sched_oracle path is already approved (my answer on K5-plan: icount + sched_oracle + the post-check hook).
> Also put both rulings in the docs commit's KERNEL-SPEC clarification (R7/R12). Post v3 consolidated on K5-plan, then complete the assignment.

> - Oscillating carve/uncarve gains nothing. Pass is a virtual-time position and weight only scales future charges; a carve folds at the old weight, so the current wait is kept (weight 1 afterwards only makes later runs dearer). A return only over-charges, which is safe.

> M1 (P1) max(parent, candidate) absorbs a churned child's work whenever the parent has its own lead.
> Attack: P (limit 100) holds a spinner thread and a churner thread, and carves C (weight 1, so P's free weight is 99). C spins for one slice, so C's lead is S/1 (S = one slice x STRIDE), which is work S.
> Near the end of P's own slice, the churner calls budget_destroy(C). R6 folds P first, so P.pass = f + about S/99. The weight returns (w_P = 100), W = S, and the candidate is f + S/100.
> max keeps P's f + S/99, so C's whole slice is forgiven. The churner then creates C' (weight 1) at max(floor, P.pass). In each cycle V (100) gets about one slice while P and C' get one each, so the attacker subtree gets about 2/3 against a fair 1/2. The same works with a C deadline set to fire just after P's slice.
> v3's proof line 'every run of a destroyed descendant ends up charged to its ancestor' fails here: max charges it only when it exceeds the parent's own lead.
> The worry that a sum double-counts applies to absolute passes, not to leads above the floor. Each lead is unpaid work beyond f, so summing leads conserves work exactly.
> Fix: after the weight returns, base = max(P.pass, f) with P.rem, and P.(pass, rem) = base + (W / w_P_new, W % w_P_new), with the carry. Not rescaling P's own lead when its weight rises only over-charges, which is safe.
> With this, the churn proof holds as written, and cross-principal lifts stay tiny: each lift into users is W/w_users, and leads decay as the floor advances.
> Tests: the current sched-budget-churn (the churner blocks while C runs, so P has no lead) and property (g) would not catch the max bug. Add a variant where the parent spins and destroys at the end of its own slice, plus a deadline-timed variant, and a mutation R12LiftByMax. Recheck sched-debt-lift under the additive rule; its bound should still hold.

> Other dying-budget arithmetic is fine. R10 kills processes before step 6, so dying budgets aren't runnable and f excludes them. A weight-0 child carries nothing, and bottom-up return means w_child equals its limit at its own destroy.

> Q1 (P1) The double-counted entry wait compounds; it is not at most one step.
> A child enters at e = max(floor, P.pass), carrying P's lead L. At destroy, W = (C.pass - f)+ x w_C still contains that L, and it is added on top of base = max(P.pass, f), which also still carries L.
> Creating and destroying with no run: P holds processes with free weight a and carves C with weight c. Then L' = L(1 + c/a), which is about 2L for c = a-1. It is geometric in the number of create/destroy pairs made before the floor decays L. The plan's bound (one parent step x w_C/w_P per destroy) assumes L is at most one step, but L itself grows with each destroy.
> Victim: honest programs. A shell or launcher that gives each short command a child budget with most of its weight grows by 1.5-2x per command, so 50 quick commands mean 10^8-10^15 x its lead of starvation. Shared parents grow by (1 + w_C/w_users or w_system) per destroy, which compounds with a crash-looping driver restart under system (about 1.004x per cycle).
> Fix: record each budget's entry position e (u128, 2 frame words) at create, and use W = (child.pass - max(e, f))+ x w_C + child.rem, counting only the child's own unpaid charges.
> - No double count: base = max(P.pass, f) >= e always, because P.pass and f are both monotone and e = max(f_create, P.pass_create).
> - M1 still closed: e ~ f, C.pass = e + S, so W = S and P = f + S/99 + S/100.
> - Parking still closed: M's pass above e_M includes C's lifted work.
> - Create/destroy with no run moves nothing.
> - The steady state is unchanged: leads above the floor are about 0.
> Add a property and mutation (e.g. R12LiftCountsEntryWait, caught by an idempotence property: create+destroy with no run leaves P's lead unchanged) and a shell-pattern check (a parent doing N quick child create/run/destroy cycles keeps its share - tol). Put the corrected formula in OWNER DECISION 6.
> 
> Closed:
> - sched-debt-lift re-check: the bound holds under either formula.
> - Carve-mid-syscall P3 (s1, s7).
> - File consistency: no superseded v1-v3 text remains. The s5 step 6 max, the O(1) claim and the stale counts are gone.
> 
> P3 notes (fine to fix during implementation):
> 1. Boot split mismatch. s4 has the kernel at users 750,000 (ROOT - ROOT/4, so root's free weight is 0), while s9/N8 has the model at 1,000,000/250,000/500,000 (root keeps 250,000). The sched-debt-lift arithmetic uses 748,000. Align the model with boot_budgets, or state the divergence. Under rule 7 root's free weight is now a stride weight, so the difference matters.
> 2. WP-K5 acceptance: 'a large-weight server keeps its share UNDER THAT LOAD'. sched-large-weight runs 1000 vs 8x100 separately, and the sched-latency row no longer asserts the share. Assert the large-weight share inside sched-latency (named workload, N=16), as v1 did.
> 3. Mutation coverage gaps. Rule 7's carve refusal and fold-at-old-weight/rem-rescale have no mutation. ProcessInWeightlessBudget should move to free weight. Add R7CarveToZeroFree and R12FoldAtNewWeight (caught by h, or a focused weight-change property).
> 4. s9 should restate that kernel-work billing (s7) is out of model and covered by sched-timer-flood; that line was dropped in consolidation.
